text.p: NEW YORK - Stocks started 1997 the way they ended 1996: falling on investor worries about higher interest rates.
Thursday's drop came after a report that showed robust manufacturing activity in December sparked a steep decline in the inflation-sensitive bond market, which in turn hurt stocks.

At 1 p.m., the Dow Jones industrial average was off 40.80 points at 6,407.47 after falling as much as 95 points earlier. In the broader market, declining issues outnumbered gainers by better than 3-1 on moderate New York Stock Exchange volume of about 266 million shares.
The drop came after the Dow fell 101 points on Tuesday.

Analysts said the declines might signal the start of a tough year for stocks. The market rose 26 percent in 1996 and 33.5 percent in 1995 as measured by the Dow, back-to-back gains seen only twice before in the market's history.

The report that sparked the sell-off came from the National Association of Purchasing Management, which said its index of maufacturing activity rose to 54.0 in December, the highest in six months, from 52.7 in November. A reading above 50 points to growth in manufacturing, while one below that level indicates contraction.

The report, the first broad glimpse of the economy each month, signalled a pickup in economic growth that could lead to accelerating inflation and higher interest rates, traders and analysts said. The group's index stood at 54.3 in June.
It was the first major indicator of the new year and had been widely awaited in financial markets. Private economists had expected a reading of 51.5 for December.

LONDON - UK shares suffered a dismal start to the New Year to end sharply lower after fresh U.S. economic data strengthened fears of inflationary pressures and spooked financial markets. The FTSE 100 index of blue-chip shares lost 61.1 points or 1.5 percent to close at 4,057.4.

FRANKFURT - German equities ended the first bourse session of 1997 down 1.38 percent after the latest 101-point fall in the Dow Jones share index, with lower German debt futures also generating negative sentiment, strong dollar underpins market, and no serious correction feared with too few players around and
volumes exceedingly thin. The DAX-30 index ended at 2,848.77 down 39.92 points. In post-bourse trade the DAX index stood at 2,820.81.

PARIS - French shares closed sharply down in thin volume, spooked by renewed fears of U.S. interest rate tightening following data suggesting a more robust than expected American economy. The blue-chip CAC-40 index ended near their late session lows, down 2.54 percent or 58.76 points at 2,256.97.
ZURICH - The Zurich stock market is closed for a National Holiday. On Tuesday the final session of 1996 the Swiss Performance Index (SPI) shed 3.74 points to 2,511.88 points.
TOKYO - The Tokyo stock market is closed for a National Holiday. On Monday the Nikkei 225 index ended the final session of 1996 down 7.69 points at 19,361.35.
HONG KONG - Hong Kong stocks closed 1.84 percent lower on jitters induced by Wall Street's 100-point plunge on New Year's Eve. The Hang Seng Index slumped 248.01 points to 13,203.44.

SYDNEY - Australian shares closed weaker but well off their lows as a thinly-traded market greeted the New Year. The All Ordinaries index shed 13.4 points to 2,411.2 after touching an intraday low of 2,397.8.

JOHANNESBURG - South African shares took a battering as New Year's cheer was replaced by a festive hangover on Wall Street, a Tuesday night 101 point drop in New York, spurred by interest rate fears, hit global markets across Asia and Europe, South African stocks did not escape the gloom.The All-share index
shed 40.6 points to 6,616.9 as the Industrial index fell 62.1 points to 7,859.5 and the Gold index lost 18.1 points to 1,488.1.
